JsonFormElements.Name: DUA
JsonFormElements.Statement:
This Data Use Agreement ("Agreement") sets the terms under which network and external investigators may access and use de-identified AlcHepNet data hosted in the AlcHepNet Alcohol Research Data Commons (ARDaC). This Agreement is consistent with the AlcHepNet’s Material Use Agreement and specifies the appropriate use of ARDaC data. 
1.	**Definitions**
- **Data**: De-identified AlcHepNet data and derived tables/figures hosted in ARDaC and managed by the Data Coordinating Center (DCC). 
- **DCC**: Indiana University Data Coordinating Center, custodian for ARDaC data access and transfer. 
- **DAR (Data Access Request)**: Application for accessing ARDaC data and services.
- **MAR (Material Access Request)**: A document requesting access to AlcHepNet material (data and biosamples). An MAR should include: 1) a formal research proposal (aims and approach); 2) funding support; 3) sample storing set up; 4) data sharing, attribution, acknowledgement, and plans for manuscript submission. MARs will be reviewed for approval by the AlcHepNet Publication & Ancillary Study Subcommittee.
- **Qualified Investigator / Approved Users**: The PI and named team members approved by DCC for access to ARDaC data and services. 
2.	**Purpose & Exploratory Use**
- Use Data solely for exploratory purposes and in compliance with applicable laws and institutional policies.
- ARDaC supports exploratory use to develop research ideas. Users may browse/profile and run preliminary feasibility analyses within ARDaC. 
- No data exportation is allowed under this DUA. To export data or receive a configured analysis workspace, please submit and obtain approval for an MAR. 
- During exploration, do not download, take screenshots, or copy any data or figures that could identify individuals or reconstruct individual record-level data. 
3.	**Terms of Use**
- Use only for exploration or the MAR-approved scope and by Approved Users.
- No re-identification, contacting participants, or redistribution to non-approved parties.
- For users with an approved MAR, changes to scope/personnel/methods require an approved MAR amendment by P&ASC. 
4.	**Access** 
- Submit a DAR to DCC for review/approval. 
- The use of ARDaC exploratory functionalities is free of charge. 
- The use of ARDaC cloud computing facilities and services may generate costs, which will be defined in additional agreements. 
5.	**Security & Compliance**
- Report suspected incidents/breaches to the DCC within 24 hours; provide a written incident report within 3 business days. 
- Approved data downloads are permitted under the AlcHepNet Material Access Agreement. 
- Obtain institutional IRB approval or exemption before export or use outside ARDaC. Institutions certify compliance (e.g., HIPAA/HITECH). 
6.	**Publication & Dissemination (Publication Committee Approval Required)**
- All manuscripts, abstracts, posters, talks, and public figures/images using AlcHepNet/ARDaC data require prior P&ASC approval.
- All tables/statistics/figures derived from ARDaC must be submitted for committee review **before external submission or presentation**.
- Acknowledgment text: "Data used in this study were obtained from the Alcohol Associated Hepatitis Network (AlcHepNet) Research Data Commons (ARDaC), funded by the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA U24 AA026969). The findings and conclusions are those of the authors and do not necessarily represent the views of AlcHepNet or NIAAA."
- Deposit analysis code/metadata needed for transparency in ARDaC upon request. A proprietary publication window may be granted at the committee’s discretion.
- Submission pathway: [system/portal/email] (e.g., publications@…).
7.	**Term & Disposition**
- Access term: **1 year**; renewable upon progress update and continued compliance. 
- At completion/termination, **destroy retained data** and confirm to the DCC, or request an extension with justification and a security plan. 
- After destruction, provide a written destruction attestation or IT ticket number. 
8.	**Intellectual Property**
- ARDaC Data are pre competitive; no IP may be claimed over the Data themselves.
- Consistent with this Agreement and NIH principles, investigators may pursue IP on downstream discoveries/methods; this Agreement does not grant rights in the underlying Materials.
- This Agreement does not transfer any ownership or control of the data.
9.	**Disclaimer & Violations**
- Data are provided “as is.” Each party is responsible for its own acts/omissions; NIH is subject to the Federal Tort Claims Act.
- Violations (e.g., unauthorized sharing, re-identification, unapproved publication) may result in immediate revocation, institutional notification, and other remedies allowed by law/policy.

JsonFormElements.Name: Confirmation
JsonFormElements.Description: By checking this box, I agree that (1) data will be used only as approved; (2) derived outputs/metadata will be returned upon request; and (3) AlcHepNet/NIAAA will be acknowledged in all publications/presentations per Section 6.

JsonFormComplianceBundleOptions.GroupDisplayDescription: All users that have an Acceptable Use Agreement are included in this group. More details about the use agreement can be found https://one.iu.edu/task/iu/acceptable-use-agreement.

IU requires training for all employees that handle or access student records to complete the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) tutorial. This group contains compliance data associated to that training. More details about the tutorial can be found https://one.iu.edu/task/iu/ferpa

Pursuant to the HIPAA Privacy & Security Rules, the HITECH Act and the IU HIPAA Privacy and Security Compliance Plan, IU must inform all of its workforce members of their responsibilities to protect PHI when using mobile devices, regardless of ownership of that device.  More details about the training can be found https://compliance.iu.edu/compliance-areas/hipaa/training.html.

The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and the IU HIPAA Privacy and Security Compliance Plan require the completion of HIPAA training annually.

Pursuant to the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules, the HITECH Act and the IU HIPAA Privacy and Security Compliance Plan, all workforce members (which includes academic appointees, staff, students, interns, residents, fellows, and affiliates) in an IU HIPAA Affected Area must complete the HIPAA training on an annual basis.

More details about the training can be found https://compliance.iu.edu/compliance-areas/hipaa/training.html.

The Human Resource Management Systems (HRMS) requires training to gain access to underlying data. This group contains compliance data associated to that training. More details about the HRMS Data Use Tutorial can be found https://one.iu.edu/task/iu/hrms-data-use-tutorial.

Membership contains all active employees, IU Foundation and students. Active employee is defined as active, not-retired, individuals that have at least one primary or secondary position at the university. Active student is defined as enrolled or currently enrolled.
